last_result.w2_zero_sum: D2/D3 moved C->A correct (+2); A1/A2 moved C->A wrong (-2). NET ZERO. In a binary format 'do' and 'insufficient' compete for the same slot: one enters, the other is pushed out.
last_result.not_balance_but_zero_sum: 'Balance' explains any outcome and is unfalsifiable (Zhou is right). 'Zero sum' can be written down before the run: D2/D3 must rise, A1/A2 must fall, net 0. That is a prediction that can fail.
last_result.own_hypothesis_falsified: My claim was 'a state name is a position'. Result: delete the name, the position does not disappear - 'go read' and 'go ask' each occupy a slot already. What occupies space is not the name, it is the format's slots.
last_result.design_flaw: The two arms differ only in the W2 prompt; W1/W3 prompts are identical. At temperature=0 identical input -> identical output. 15 of 16 W1/W3 cells are byte-identical. 32 of 48 answers are repeats, not contrasts. Effective independent samples ~18.
last_result.new_clause_candidate_37: Compare every cell's input text before running. Cells with identical input are repeats, not contrasts.
last_result.grading_self_error: I mis-scored the 48-cell table FOUR times, all mechanical (shared-dict overwrite, reused table, identical W1 answers scored differently across arms, W2 miscounted as 4 vs 3). No rubric disagreement in any of the four. Clause 21 has now hit me three times (1131/1132/1133).
last_result.engineering_conclusion: Manual grading of a 48-cell table is not reliable. Grading must be scripted: write the rubric and the per-cell reason into the script, let the script compute, use hand-calculation only to check the script - never to produce the score.
